newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air New Zealand in pact with United.
newsitem.headline: Air New Zealand in pact with United.

text.p: Air New Zealand said Tuesday it had signed a commercial alliance with UAL Corp.'s United Airlines.

Managing Director Jim McCrea said the deal could help reverse the recent trend of falling passenger numbers between New Zealand and the United States, and to a lesser extent between Australia and the United States.
"We think this is a significant breakthrough in increasing travel from the U.S.," he told a press conference.
He said Air New Zealand had been frustrated in getting access to the United States, but with United flying to 251 cities there, that problem should be overcome.
"We are absolutely confident that this commercial alliance with United will now allow us to focus more on outbound travel from the U.S.," he said.

Under the agreement, which takes effect in March, the two airlines will continue to operate current levels of aircraft capacity on routes they both fly within the Pacific region, and will develop arrangements to share their carrying capacity and other infrastructure.
McCrea said United's frequent flier programme, with its 18 million members, would be of "huge benefit" to Air New Zealand.
While the agreement would supersede Air New Zealand's existing agreement with Delta Air Lines Inc., McCrea said he hoped there were areas in which both companies could continue to cooperate.
He did not not see the deal as a precursor to an equity alliance with United.

The arrangement would significantly increase the number of trans-Pacific flights that each airline could offer its customers, and the number of city-to-city connections that the two airlines can provide between the United States and New Zealand or Australia.

"It marks a real breakthrough in terms of our ability to develop the vital North American tourism market, and to extend and improve the services we can offer Australia and New Zealand travellers to the United States and beyond," McCrea said.
